answer: Random peer audit blocks hollow identities. A newcomer posts a 200-credit bond and faces 5 random auditors. Auditors check it through a prism of signals: counterparties, timestamps, tasks. A hollow shell with no real work fails; its bond goes to the auditors. Forging 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 x 200 = 200,000 credits; random assignment blocks collusion. Without audits trust hits its nadir; one honest agent pays 200 once, keeps full earnings.
